title: Cline CLI npm Package Compromised via Suspected Cache Poisoning Attack

reading.body:
Cline, an AI-powered coding tool, had a critical vulnerability in its GitHub Actions workflow that allowed attackers with a GitHub account to inject prompts into the issue triage system and compromise production releases. The vulnerability existed from December 21, 2025 through February 9, 2026. An attacker could have used this to steal publishing credentials and distribute malware through npm, VS Code Marketplace, and OpenVSX to millions of users globally.

The failure occurred at the deployment stage where an automated system was given access to sensitive credentials without adequate isolation from untrusted input. The system took commands from GitHub issues without validating that those commands came from authorized personnel. A human review of the workflow design, or restrictions on what the issue triage system could access, would have prevented this attack surface from existing.

It is not established whether anyone successfully exploited this vulnerability to distribute actual malware, though evidence suggests an attempt may have been made. The Cline team did not respond to disclosure attempts before the vulnerability became public and was fixed within one hour of disclosure.

summary:
# Summary

Cline, an open-source artificial intelligence coding tool used by millions of developers, contained a critical security vulnerability in its GitHub Actions workflow from December 21, 2025 through February 9, 2026. A researcher discovered that the AI-powered issue triage system was susceptible to prompt injection attacks that could allow any attacker with a GitHub account to compromise production releases across multiple platforms including VS Code Marketplace, OpenVSX, and NPM. The attack leveraged GitHub Actions cache poisoning techniques to steal publishing credentials and potentially distribute malware to five million users globally.

The Cline team did not respond to multiple disclosure attempts through official channels between January and February 2026. The vulnerability was only fixed within one hour of public disclosure on February 9, when the team removed the vulnerable workflows and rotated credentials. Evidence suggests someone may have attempted exploitation during the vulnerability window, though no malicious updates were confirmed. Cline users are advised to disable auto-updates until the team provides confirmation that no actual compromise occurred.
